tagline: From the badlands floor to the rim, then back again
intro: The North Unit Scenic Drive runs 14 miles into the badlands, climbing from the canyon floor to the rim before ending at Oxbow Overlook. The National Park Service recommends at least an hour and 15 minutes for the 28-mile round trip. North Dakota Tourism presents the scenic byway as a route through open prairie and wooded draws, with the Little Missouri River and opportunities to see wildlife. Bison are often visible from the drive at any hour of the day.

Civilian Conservation Corps camps worked in both future park units from 1934 to 1941, building roads and structures that remain in use. The North Unit joined Theodore Roosevelt National Memorial Park in 1948. Congress established the Theodore Roosevelt Wilderness in 1978, when the park also received its present national-park designation. The landscape’s wildlife also reflects park management: twenty bison were transferred from the South Unit herd to the North Unit in 1962.

Enter from US 85 south of Watford City and travel west along the scenic drive. The first half follows the bottom of the badlands before climbing to River Bend Overlook. The remaining drive follows the rim to Oxbow, then returns by the same road. The surface is almost entirely paved, with one gravel stretch.

moments.title: Buckhorn Trail
moments.text: The Buckhorn Trail leaves the driving tour for an eleven-mile loop through the North Unit. It begins and ends at a parking lot directly across from the North Unit campground. Buckhorn is one of the backcountry trails that traverse the park’s wilderness areas. In this unit, seeing prairie dogs requires a hike, while bison are often visible from the scenic drive. The National Park Service asks visitors to keep a safe distance from wildlife.

moments.title: River Bend Overlook
moments.text: River Bend Overlook marks the climb out of the canyon, midway along the scenic drive. Its Civilian Conservation Corps shelter connects the view with the park’s early development. CCC camps operated in both future park units between 1934 and 1941, developing roads and other structures still used today. That work preceded the North Unit’s addition to the memorial park in 1948. Beyond the overlook, the road continues along the badlands rim toward Oxbow.
moments.notice: The CCC shelter accompanies the view at River Bend Overlook.

moments.title: Oxbow Overlook
moments.text: Oxbow Overlook is the end of the road, reached along the badlands rim. Most of the North Unit belongs to the wilderness Congress established in 1978. The protected terrain includes steep cliffs carved into prairie by erosion. The Little Missouri River is the principal erosional force behind that landscape. The scenic drive is an out-and-back route, so Oxbow also marks the turn for the return journey.
